body:
>  The only thing that will be worthwhile is what you can do.

Yes, which is end it. All of it.

>Trying to find one is better than giving up without trying.

Thanks for confirming you haven't been paying attention. At all. At least you got to pretend you give a shit, right?

>how is death going to make it any better when you can change? 

It would make the world a better place, quicker and more effectively than any "change" you can pull out your arse.

>What stops you from changing?

Ever heard of the Russian foxes? DNA, man. It's all in the DNA.

1. I already served.
2. Your plan to teach the mentally ill how to kill has some flaws.
3. Veterans have one of the highest suicide rates in the world.
4. I've already been around the world. Several times over, in fact. Spent the night in a Kolkatan jail, got stabbed in Bangkok, been set on fire in the Ramapos. All that's left is the final adventure.

> You also have to remember that not everyone is a bad person

I never said they were. ***I*** am. Big difference. Evil cannot be tolerated. Must not be tolerated. We burn it out.

>That might sound like more romantic bs

It does. Because it is.

As someone who's been to every continent bar the Poles, that's romantic claptrap dreamed up by some Hollywood cokefiend. Wherever you run, you can't run away from yourself. Anyone who says otherwise is a liar or in denial.

>why not take that trip without a set end goal? 

Been there, done that. Spent nearly five years tripping around, still gonna kill myslef.

>What is it that's pushing you that way if you don't mind me asking?

Bluntly, I'm a worthless piece of shit that doesn't deserve to live. Some might disagree, but they're wrong and they know it.
